scenes.headline: How TrackEverything tracks every point of a long video
scenes.sub: Memory that grows with the scene, not with the frame count
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Quillon! Here's how Track Everything follows every point through a thousand frames.

scenes.text: Keep one track per piece of surface in world coordinates, and merge tracks that land in the same voxel.
scenes.mark: merge tracks that land in the same voxel
scenes.say: Keep one track per piece of surface. Tracks that land in the same voxel are one surface: merge them.

left.title: Frame-local tokens
items: Every frame adds a full grid
left.say: A frame-local tracker adds a full grid of tokens every frame, new or not. Memory grows with video length.

right.title: De-duplicated scene memory
items: A surface seen again lands in an existing voxel
Memory grows only with new surface
right.say: Here, a surface seen again lands in a voxel that already exists. Memory grows only with new surface.

steps.say: Sixteen frames arrive with a point in space for every pixel, and their features are lifted into one cloud in world coordinates.
The endpoint refiner guesses where each point ends up, and whether it moves, by sampling features where the guess lands.
Only moving points get a full path, frame by frame. Static points keep their place.
Then points that land in the same voxel merge. Two things can't be in one place at one time.
The survivors are the scene memory, and the next window joins them.

parts.note: carried memory: grows only with never-seen surface
parts.say: Carried memory grows only with the part of each frame that's never been seen.

parts.note: the window in flight: 16 frames, a constant
parts.say: The window in flight adds a constant, whatever the video's length.

steps.say: In the paper, one boundary turns forty-six thousand points into sixteen thousand.

scenes.title: Decode only the moving points
scenes.note: seconds per frame; 31.2 APD-P either way
scenes.say: Splitting static from moving points keeps accuracy identical and cuts time per frame almost five times.

scenes.label: peak memory at 896 frames, one L40S
scenes.say: Read off the paper's plot: under fifteen gigabytes at nearly nine hundred frames.

scenes.text: Memory should follow the scene, not the clock: store each surface once, and pay for motion only where it happens.
scenes.say: Store each surface once, and pay for motion only where it happens.

recap: Merge tracks that share a voxel
Decode paths only for moving points
Sample features instead of correlation volumes
scenes.say: Merge what shares a voxel, decode only what moves, and sample features instead of correlation volumes.
